cp.title: PS2 Elite: what every column means
cp.sub: Short answers, one column at a time. Hover any number on the main page for details. Back to the stats · Update log · Formulas: docs/metrics.md
cp.curveAria: Your K/D drawn against opponent strength: high against easy opponents on the left, lower against hard opponents on the right.
cp.idea1: Most ✨ columns read this line: your K/D against opponents from easy (left) to hard (right). It uses the ~200 players you fight most, not your whole career.
cp.idea2: Why it matters: a player can show 3.96 lifetime K/D and only 1.15 against the people he really fights.
cp.whyH: Why Honu and Fisu don’t show these
cp.whyP: They look up one player. These columns also need the stats of your ~200 opponents, so this site keeps them all cached and refreshed. The 📊 Census / Fisu / Honu style columns are the same numbers the trackers show.
cp.iviP: How good you are, once your opponents’ strength is counted.
cp.iviL1: Beating strong players counts more than beating weak ones.
cp.iviL2: Fast killing adds a bonus; slow, safe play costs a little.
cp.iviL3: Infantry only: vehicle and MAX kills above 10% lower it (🚜). Confirmed padders lose 10% (💩).
cp.iviL4: PlayStation: the 600 baseline is divided by the PC/PlayStation kill-speed gap (rechecked weekly), so top players compare fairly with PC.
cp.iviHigh: High: you beat strong players at a good pace.
cp.iviLow: Low: your wins come from weak players, or you play slowly. Below zero shows as 0.
cp.actP: Your ☠️ K/D × how fast you kill.
cp.actHigh: High: lots of fights won, quickly.
cp.actLow: Low: you lose more than you win, or you kill slowly.
cp.braveH: 🦁 Brave — does it hold against strong players?
cp.braveP: Your 🏃 Activity, checked against the fastest-killing enemies you meet.
cp.braveHigh: High: you stay strong when the enemy gets strong.
cp.braveLow: Low with a high iVi: you pick easy fights and avoid even ones.
cp.bravePs: PlayStation: enemy kill speeds and your 🏃 Activity are multiplied by the PC/PlayStation kill-speed gap (rechecked weekly) before 🦁 Brave is worked out, so top players compare fairly with PC.
cp.resH: 🛡️ Resist — K/D, weighted by enemy danger
cp.resP: Your ☠️ K/D × how fast your enemies kill. 1.0 K/D against killers is worth more than 1.0 against beginners. ⚔️ iVi is built from it.
cp.resHigh: High: you hold your own against fast killers.
cp.resLow: Low: your K/D comes from slower enemies.
cp.constH: ⚡ Const — do you hold up at the hard end?
cp.constP: Your K/D in the hard third ÷ your K/D in the easy third of the picture above (max 1). Shown as a percentile.
cp.constHigh: High (line stays flat): you do as well against hard opponents as easy ones.
cp.constLow: Low (line drops): you farm easy opponents and struggle against hard ones.
cp.constNote: Catch: someone equally weak everywhere also scores high, so Const is only a colour hint, never a rating.
cp.kdH: ☠️ K/D — against people you actually fight
cp.kdP: Kills ÷ deaths against your ~200 most-fought players. Not your lifetime K/D. Every ✨ column starts from this.
cp.kdHigh: High: you win most of those fights.
cp.kdLow: Low: you die more than you kill.
cp.infP: % of your lifetime kills made with infantry weapons. MAX counts as infantry here; vehicles, turrets and roadkills don’t. Shown from 100 kills (“—” until measured). Hover for your MAX and vehicle shares.
cp.infTractor: 🚜 Vehicle: a 🚜 appears next to your name, like 🪦, when you mostly play in vehicles. It works like 🪳, and every line is taken from the data at each build: your infantry share is in the lowest quarter of all ranked players (below about 71.9%) and your Honu XP shows a lot of vehicle repairs or vehicle kills per minute (top quarter of players with 2+ hours of XP detail); or your infantry share is in the lowest 2% (below about 21.7%), even without XP detail. Hover it for the hint; the Infantry number itself does not change. On 🎥 LIVE the 🪖 turns into 🚜 below that infantry cut and fills: almost empty just under the cut, full (and shiny) at half the cut (about 36%) or less. Between the cut and the median (about 85.1%) the 🪖 stays empty; above the median it fills up to 100% infantry. Not the same as the 🚜 vehicle cut on ⚔️ iVi or the 🔀🚜 Diff reduction: this mark changes no number.
cp.vcP: The first 10% of vehicle kills are free; every % above costs 1% of iVi. MAX kills work the same way, separately. The two add up.
cp.vcNote: Why: farming infantry from a tank, aircraft or MAX is easier than on foot. Hover the iVi value to see the cut. The site owner can exempt a player.
cp.pdP: Players confirmed farming kills on their own or friendly alt accounts get 💩 and lose 10% of iVi (kills on farm accounts are already left out). Hover 💩 for the reason. Think it’s wrong? Contact the site owner.
cp.pubH: 📊 Census / Fisu / Honu style (the tracker numbers)
cp.pubSub: Lifetime numbers from Census, no adjustment. The same ones Honu and Fisu show.
cp.pubKd: Kills ÷ deaths over your whole career, against everyone. Flatters players who farm weak opponents.
cp.pubKpm: Kills per minute over your whole career.
cp.pubOwn: Kills per minute with your own weapons. Drives the iVi pace bonus or cut.
cp.pubAcc: Share of your shots that hit.
cp.pubHsr: Share of your kills that were headshots.
cp.pubIvi: Census’s lifetime infantry score, with no opponent weighting. Compare it with ⚔️ iVi (see the example).
cp.exNameAria: Character name for the example (type any cached name)
cp.dbgP: Older or in-between numbers. Tick “show older debug stats” in the main page footer to see them. Not used to judge anyone.
cp.dbgMech: A guess of your vehicle / mech share, projected from 🛡️ Resist. Not measured.
cp.dbgIvi: ⚔️ iVi before the pace bonus or cut, so slow play still looks good.
cp.dbgEkpm: How fast your opponents kill, on average. Higher = harder opposition.
cp.dbgOwn: Same as the 📊 Census / Fisu / Honu style column.
cp.dbgSlope: The angle of your line. Negative = your K/D drops against harder enemies. Feeds 🦁 Brave.
cp.dbgInfl: Lifetime KD ÷ KD against enemies killing at 0.5+ per minute. Above 1 = easy fights inflate your KD. Lower is better.
cp.dbgZchg: ⚔️ iVi evened out for 🪳 Zerg: (iVi + 3100) × e^(−0.00021 × (🪳 − 26.8)) − 3100. Measured on 103,689 duel pairs: at the same iVi, each 🪳 step costs about 0.08% of kills in duels, about the same number of points in every tier. no 🪳 = unchanged (players without 🪳 duel like 🪳 26.8); at iVi 1,000, 🪳 0 → +23, 🪳 50 → −20, 🪳 99 → −62. No vehicle part: the 🚜 cut already handles vehicles. PC only.

cp.zergRevive: Crowd check: where we have Honu XP detail (50+ deaths, 2+ h), we count per death the revives, heals, shield repairs and ammo you received, plus engineer Hardlight barrier XP (it only ticks inside a big crowd). Zergs die in a crowd, so the crowd picks them up. Revives or the crowd score in the top quarter = Zerg confirmed (hover says so). Both in the bottom half = a high Zerg is softened step by step. Never raised. No 🪳 Zerg but a top-quarter crowd score = an estimate “~N”, shown only, never sorted or marked. No XP detail = no change.
cp.zergGap: Apr 1 – May 6, 2026 is skipped for 🤝 Assists and 🪳 Zerg: a game bug recorded no assists then (fixed May 6). Too few kills left = “—”.
cp.diffVeh: Vehicle damp: above the typical vehicle share (about 15% of kills), a positive Diff counts only in proportion to your kills on foot (46% vehicle → ×0.63, 76% → ×0.28). If 🛖 also applies, only the stronger cut counts. Hover the Diff value to see it.
nbd.note: Short play time: a negative Diff is softened (new players are still learning).
nbd.explain: 🐣 New player: a negative 🔀 Diff counts less for players with few hours.
diff.nbdFrom: 🐣 Softened from {raw} (short play time: still learning).
cp.diffNewbie: Newbie softening: a negative Diff is scaled by estimated play time (lifetime kills ÷ lifetime KPM). About 6 h or less (the newest 5% of players) → 0; then it rises smoothly to the full value at about 385 h (the median player). New accounts are still learning, so they are not called 🤥 Impostors yet. Positive Diff is untouched. Hover the Diff value to see it.

priv.title: PS2 Elite: privacy
priv.sub: The short version. Full details: PRIVACY.md · data sources: DATA_SOURCES.md
priv.players1: Characters shown here come from public game data (Daybreak Census API and Honu): name and id, outfit, stats, weapons, opponents and login times. Nothing else: no real names, emails or locations. We don't know who plays a character.
priv.players2: Why: community stats, rankings and fair-play checks. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)).
priv.players3: Ratings and marks are automated estimates, not facts or accusations. Think a mark on your character is wrong? Open an issue for a human review.
priv.remove1: Don't want your character here? Remove it yourself below. We delete our copy, stop fetching it, take it out of Rankings and other players' opponent lists, and show “removed at the player's request” instead.
priv.remove2: Only the player can do this: you prove the character is yours by logging out once in the game. Can't sign in? Delete the character in the game, or ask Daybreak support to delete your account: once Daybreak no longer has it, our copy is deleted automatically within about two days. We only keep what Daybreak publishes; we can't remove it from Daybreak or other sites.
priv.v1: No cookies, no analytics, no ads, no trackers.
priv.v2: Your browser keeps your settings and cached stats on your device only. “Clear local data” in the footer deletes them.
priv.v3: Live stats come straight from Daybreak's servers to your browser, so Daybreak sees your IP address.
priv.v4: GitHub (hosting) and Cloudflare (our two small servers) see IP addresses. We store them only as a scrambled code for rate limits, for about an hour.
priv.oracle1: Signing in stores your character, a sign-in token per device (a phone can join with a one-time QR code from your signed-in PC), your BonusCheques (no cash value) and your votes. Sign-in attempts and QR codes are deleted after a day. Ask in an issue to delete your account.
priv.k1: Player stats: while the character exists, or until you ask for removal.
priv.k4: Older copies stay in the public Git history of the project.
priv.rights1: Access, correction, objection, deletion: open an issue; we answer within a month. You can also complain to your data protection authority. Security problems: SECURITY.md.

cp.iviL5: PC: evened out for 🪳 Zerg: low 🪳 goes up a little, high 🪳 down, the average crowd (🪳 26.8) stays.
cp.zaP: Fighting inside a big crowd lifts the numbers a little beyond what you win on your own. We measured how much on real fights, take exactly that back, and give it to players who fight with less help.
cp.zaL1: Measured, not guessed: 103,689 pairs of players who fought each other 30+ times. At the same ⚔️ iVi, each 🪳 step means about 0.08% fewer kills against the other player.
cp.zaL2: Both ways: 🪳 below 26.8 (the average crowd, where players without a 🪳 score fight) goes up, above it goes down. At iVi 1,000: 🪳 0 → +23, 🪳 50 → −20, 🪳 99 → −62.
cp.zaL3: Checked on players it never saw: fitted on half the players and tested on the other half, the 🪳 bias in their fights disappeared and fight predictions got slightly better.
cp.zaL4: Same weight in every tier; most players move by 1% or less. No 🪳 score or PlayStation → unchanged. Vehicles are not counted twice: the 🚜 cut already handles them. Away for 60+ days (no recent sessions) → unchanged until a refresh brings fresh data.
cp.zaNote: Research and numbers: docs/zerg-adjustment.md · discussion: issue #84. Hover ⚔️ iVi to see your before → after.
cp.pureiviH: 🧘‍♂️ Pure iVi — your true solo ability
cp.pureiviP: What your rating would be if every fight counted as if you fought alone. A high iVi on a zerg surfer says: you have it only because of crowd efforts. Pure iVi says: this is your true ability as a solo player.
cp.pureiviL1: Formula: adjs above 0 → adjs × (1 − 0.00436 × 🪳); adjs at or below 0 → adjs − 0.00436 × 🪳 × 610.6. Each 🪳 point costs about 0.44% of the rating; 🪳 100 → −43.6%.
cp.pureiviL2: Measured, not guessed: fitted on 915 duel pairs (723 infantry-only). At the same adjs gap, each 🪳 point of gap meant 0.286 fewer kill-gap points against 0.656 per adjs point — 0.286 ÷ 0.656 ≈ 0.00436.
cp.pureiviNote: Not a replacement for ⚔️ iVi, and not the 🪳⚔️ evening-out: that one centers on the average crowd (🪳 26.8) and lifts low-🪳 players up; Pure only ever discounts, never boosts, and has no freshness gate. PC only; no 🪳 score → “—”.
cp.combinediviH: 🧼 Pure — your true solo ability, cleaned twice
cp.combinediviP: What your rating would be if every fight counted as if you fought alone, and your K/D had to hold up against the fastest killers too. Pure iVi takes the crowd out; this takes the crowd and the cheese out.
cp.combinediviL1: Formula: 🧘 Pure iVi × (1 − 🌈 G), where Pure iVi is adjs × (1 − 0.00436 × 🪳). The base is the Pure value — never the displayed (🪳-evened) ⚔️ iVi, or 🪳 gets charged twice.
cp.combinediviL2: Chosen, not measured: G is the share of cached players you beat on K/D and Brave at once — a rank share, not a cheating probability. Nothing in the data says 1% of G equals 1% of your score; that rate is a choice. The 🪳 half is measured (fitted on 915 duel pairs).
cp.combinediviL3: Example: Eyfia — Pure 921 at G 9.1% → 921 × (1 − 0.091) ≈ 838. Aekris — Pure 2667 at G 99.3% → 19.
cp.combinediviNote: Not a replacement for ⚔️ iVi. 🪳 and G are near-independent (r ≈ −0.06), so stacking them docks each sin once. PC only; no 🪳 score or no G → “—”.
cp.gH: 🌈 G — how cheesy is this K/D?
cp.gP: The share of all cached players you beat on K/D and Brave at once. A high K/D alone doesn't do it — you also need a collapsed 🦁 Brave. 🪖 Infantry doesn't score anymore: it only lives in the gate — the cheesy set is Brave under 1.7 and Infantry under 50%. The 1.7 is the trimmed mean 🦁 Brave of the top 100 by K/D on PC — the typical Brave of a top-K/D player (the raw mean, 6.68, is wrecked by two outliers at 461 and 41). On PlayStation the same figure is 2.9 (raw mean 3.17, top two at 19.24 and 13.05).
cp.gL1: Formula: (1 − K/D rank) × (1 − Brave rank), ranks over all cached players. Each factor is the share of players you beat on that one dimension.
cp.gNote: Most players sit at 10–23% (median 17.21%); 90% are under 28.95%. The top 100 start at 70.09%. — a different world from the rest.

cp.dbgSore: Share of measured players you beat on revenge kills, as a percentage — the top player reads 100%, a player with no revenge kills reads 0%. The Revenge Kill XP tick. Higher means you avenge your deaths more often; it runs with lower K/D, since revenge needs a death first.

cp.apkL1: Formula: assists ÷ kills in recent Honu sessions. An assist is a kill-assist XP tick (ids 2, 3, 371, 372) — you damaged the enemy and a teammate finished them.

cp.infL1: Formula: foot kills ÷ all lifetime kills. Foot means kills with infantry weapons; MAX counts as infantry, vehicles, turrets and roadkills don’t.

adad.title: 🎯 Ideal ADAD calculator
adad.sub: Your cone of fire only grows by a fixed amount per shot, and it can never drop below the minimum cone of the stance you're in. Fire the free shots still, then strafe — once your cone reaches the moving minimum, moving costs nothing.
adad.ver.label: Data version
adad.ver.histNote: Historical version: Toolbox v6h data, Aug 2018 — the old stats and mechanics. Switch to it anytime to see the numbers Iridar's readers used; the calculator, the table and the worked examples all follow the switch.
adad.banner.cur: Current data — cone and bloom numbers from the Census snapshot of {date}. The method is the same as Iridar's; only the numbers are today's.
adad.banner.hist: Stale data warning — the weapon table below comes from Iridar's Toolbox v6h, whose Stats sheet is dated 19 August 2018 — before later rebalances and redesigns. Treat every preloaded number as history, not current stats. The method is timeless; the data is not. Every parameter in the calculator is editable, so type in today's numbers for any gun and the math still holds.
adad.in.rpmHint: Used for the still-window and reset timing.
adad.in.maxHintHist: The reset clamp. Not stored in the Toolbox — leave blank if you don't know it.
adad.in.maxHintCur: The reset clamp. Filled in from Census when the weapon is loaded.
adad.verdict.empty: Enter still minimum, moving minimum and bloom per shot to get the count.
adad.verdict.inf: Bloom is 0 — the cone never grows while you fire, so every still shot is free. Moving just jumps the cone straight to the moving minimum whenever you choose to start.
adad.verdict.zero: No free shots: the moving minimum is at or below the still minimum, so strafe from the very first shot — moving costs no accuracy at all.
adad.verdict.n: Fire the first {n} shots standing still, then start strafing. Your cone reaches the moving minimum exactly as you start to move, so the rest of the burst costs nothing.
adad.verdict.leftover: Switching lifts the cone by the leftover {rem}° — less than one bloom step — to reach the moving floor; the first {n} shots were still fired at full still accuracy.
adad.formula.n: floor((moving min − still min) ÷ bloom) = floor(({move} − {still}) ÷ {bloom}) = floor({ratio}) = {n}
adad.reset.line: Refire {refire}; recovery starts after one refire, then the cone shrinks at 20°/s down to the still minimum. Full reset takes about {total}.
adad.reset.clamp: Standing still clamps the bloomed cone instantly to the still maximum ({max}°) first.
adad.table.sub: Still-shot counts use the standing values. Tap any row to load that weapon into the calculator, where you can also switch to its crouching numbers. Expand a row (▸) for all four stances and its worked burst; Compare opens the in-depth comparison. Loss @ 35 m and Loss @ 60 m show how much damage strafing the whole burst costs vs the ideal rhythm at each distance — the same numbers as the calculator's “What it costs” panel, with the ideal rhythm's own cost vs standing still underneath. A dash means there is no usable value for that gun — nothing has been filled in.
adad.cost.intro: Same burst, counted in hits instead of cone size. “Miss” is the share of the 10 shots that miss a 0.5 m torso; damage is proportional to hits, so the loss is a DPS loss too.
adad.cost.loss: At {dist} m, strafing the whole burst loses {loss}% of your damage vs the ideal rhythm. The ideal rhythm itself costs {free}% vs standing still — the movement is nearly free.
adad.cost.caveat: A 10-round burst at the stance and posture above, against a 0.5 m circle — a rough torso. This counts cone spread only, not the gun climbing off target (recoil), so the real loss is bigger.
adad.cost.legend.moving: Strafing the whole burst — loss vs the ideal rhythm
adad.cost.legend.ideal: Ideal rhythm — loss vs standing still
adad.att.note: Only the attachments that change the cone or the bloom are listed, one part per slot: a barrel part and a rail part can be fitted together, two barrel parts cannot.
adad.att.none: No attachment changes this gun's numbers — nothing it can mount touches the cone or the bloom.

adad.table.note: “Free” = shots you can fire standing still before strafing costs nothing. Weapons with 0 bloom (most shotguns) never grow their cone while firing, so every still shot is free — shown as “no bloom” rather than a count.
adad.notes.h: The reset, and the fine print
adad.notes.reset: Resetting the cone: stop firing and recovery begins after a delay of one refire time (60,000 ÷ RPM milliseconds), then the cone shrinks at 20° per second down to your current stance's minimum. Standing still also clamps a bloomed cone instantly down to the still maximum CoF — famously small on the Naginata — but the 2018 Toolbox data doesn't store maximum CoF for any stance, so in the historical version that value is unknown unless you type it into the calculator yourself; the current Census data fills it in.
adad.notes.direction: Direction changes: the free-shot count is your gun's clock. How often you flip direction is the enemy's clock — forum math on strafe speeds puts a useful flip at well under a second per direction, kept unpredictable. This page computes the gun side only.
adad.notes.ns11cHist: NS-11C discrepancy, flagged honestly: Iridar's article text credits the NS-11C with 5 free ADS shots, but the v6h sheet's own numbers for it (still 0.1, moving 0.25, bloom 0.05) compute to 3. The table shows what the sheet computes; the article was likely written against older stats.
adad.notes.ns11cCur: NS-11C, current numbers: the Census snapshot gives the same sheet values (still 0.1, moving 0.25, bloom 0.05), which compute to 3 free ADS shots — the 2018 sheet and today's data agree, and both disagree with the 5 in Iridar's article text.
adad.notes.rounding: Rounding: counts are floored — a fractional shot doesn't exist. If the cone lands exactly on the moving minimum, that shot counts as free, matching Iridar's TRAC-5 example (4 shots: 0.1 + 4 × 0.05 = 0.3).
adad.foot: Method paraphrased from Iridar's Weapon Mechanics guide (archived copy). Weapon data extracted from the Stats sheet of Iridar's Toolbox v6h (Stats sheet dated 2018-08-19). Current data from the Census API via the site's weapon snapshot. Worked examples verified by hand: TRAC-5 ADS (0.3 − 0.1) ÷ 0.05 = 4 free shots; NSX Naginata ADS (0.4 − 0.15) ÷ 0.06 = 4.17 → 4 free shots.

arc.title: 📚 Archive
arc.sub: The CMDRCyrious / Iridar PlanetSide 2 knowledge archive — preserved here because the original is vanishing.
arc.whatP: A preservation archive of the PlanetSide 2 knowledge base that CMDRCyrious hosted at cmdrcyrious.com — above all, Iridar's work: the Weapon Mechanics guide, the Construction System guide, the “Highly Technical” analysis method, the Weapon Analysis Toolbox, and the videos. CMDRCyrious spent years hosting and preserving Iridar's guides, tools, and videos; this archive takes over that role. We are the knowledge database now.
arc.whyP: The data is vanishing while we watch. On 2026-11-09, when this archive was made, the live site still answered HTTP 200 for every page — but 64 of its 159 pages served no article body at all in their static HTML: navigation shell, empty content. Of those 64, 51 were recovered from the Wayback Machine and 1 (Weapon Mechanics) was already held as a 2023 snapshot; 12 pages have no Wayback snapshot anywhere and their text is lost. That is the state of the record as of 2026-11-09, and the reason this archive exists.
arc.whoP: Someone looking for this information 10 years from now. Every entry is written to stand on its own: original author and date, source URL, snapshot or archive date, what the item is, its lineage (who built on whom), and its currency status — still working, outdated, dead, or lost — with the verification date where one is known. No entry assumes you were here when it was made.
arc.lin1: Iridar (2016–2018) wrote the Weapon Mechanics guide, the Construction System guide, the “Highly Technical” analysis method, the Weapon Analysis Toolbox spreadsheet, and the angular-size research. He also made the videos.
arc.lin2: CMDRCyrious hosted and preserved Iridar's work on cmdrcyrious.com — guides, Toolbox, videos, the Weapon Simulator — and added his own highly-technical weapon guides, mechanics explainers, and calculators on top of it.
arc.lin3: Halospud wrote the Infantry Guide that CMDRCyrious linked from his infantry-guides page; it credits Iridar and teaches the movement layer Iridar's numbers don't cover.
arc.lin4: EmperorDorf (2022–2023) built the Weapon Surgeon simulator on Iridar's Toolbox stats — his stats page is Iridar's Toolbox data. His projectile-radius finding (0.03 m) then corrected Iridar's angular-size research, closing the exact in-game vs model gap Iridar himself had found and published in 2017.
arc.lin5: This archive (2026-11-09) takes over CMDRCyrious's preservation role, because the live site is already losing pages.
arc.linAngular: The angular-size correction runs through the whole collection: Iridar's angular-size research predicted headshot rates from target angular size. In 2017 he tested it himself in VR and found 57% headshots observed against 44% predicted. In that same thread, u/BoatsFriends proposed the projectile-size hypothesis; Iridar confirmed a large bullet hitbox. In 2023 Dorf quantified it: a 0.03 m projectile radius reproduces Iridar's numbers exactly. Anything here built on angular size is dead for that reason, and is marked so. The replacement is Dorf's method: simulate with a 0.03 m projectile radius.

arc.coreHalospud: Supporting material: Halospud's Infantry Guide — Part 2: Shooting Mechanics and 1v1 Basics and Part 4: Movement Tricks — teaches the movement layer the numbers don't cover.
arc.toolP: Iridar's Weapon Analysis Toolbox, v6h (2018-08-19), as CMDRCyrious hosted it. Dorf's Weapon Surgeon stats page is this data, and the Ideal ADAD Calculator computes its still-shot counts from this sheet. Download it here — the original upload link is one of the things that can vanish next.
arc.invNote: “Live” means the live site's own HTML still contained the article on 2026-11-09. “Wayback” means the live copy was empty and the text was recovered from a Wayback snapshot (date in the file's header). “Lost” means neither source has it.
arc.lostP: Checked via the Wayback availability API and the CDX API on 2026-11-09. These texts are unrecoverable from any source tried. Each page still holds what survives of it — usually just the title and page metadata.
arc.pendP: Two things were not captured when this archive was made. The Angular Size post was pending too, until it was saved by hand later the same day — it is in the inventory above. What is still missing: transcripts for both Iridar videos. YouTube rate-limited the transcript fetch (HTTP 429) and blocks this IP range for transcripts. Titles and channels are confirmed via oEmbed; the video records above carry the content notes. If you are reading this later, try the video pages in a normal browser first.
arc.methP: Inventoried from the site's sitemaps (170 URLs; 159 PlanetSide 2 pages kept, 11 non-PS2 skipped). Every kept page's raw HTML was downloaded from the live site; 64 of 159 had empty bodies, 51 were recovered from the Wayback Machine (trust the CDX API, not the availability API — it falsely reported 45 pages as having no snapshot), and 33 Wayback downloads arrived gzip-encoded and had to be gunzipped in place. HTML was converted to markdown with trafilatura; the two Halospud Google Docs came from the Docs export endpoint. Nothing here was republished or uploaded anywhere else; this is a local archive, now hosted on this site. The full method notes and inventory live in the repo at archive/src/INDEX.md.
